notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; it was correct (6 LEDs, 6 x 220 ohm resistors, 6 blue signal wires, 1 GND wire, 6 black cathode jumpers, breadboard, Uno).

Each channel: Uno pin (7,6,5,4,3,2) -> blue wire -> breadboard column in the lower half -> resistor across the centre gap -> same column in the upper half -> LED anode; the LED cathode sits in the next column and a black jumper links it to the top ground rail; the rail is wired to Uno GND.
Columns from the image: resistor/anode columns 7,10,13,16,19,22 and cathode columns 8,11,14,17,20,23, for pins 7,6,5,4,3,2 respectively.

The image labels the top half rows j-f and the bottom half rows e-a, but the catalogue names the top half 't' (rows a-e) and the bottom half 'b' (rows f-j). I used the catalogue naming: the half with the LEDs is 't' and the half with the blue wires is 'b'. Row letters within a strip are arbitrary because the strip is one node.
The top ground rail is written as tn.<n>. The exact hole numbers on the rail are approximate, because every rail hole is the same strip.
The tutorial does not say which Uno GND pin is used. The image shows the GND pin on the digital header next to AREF, and I used GND.1 for it.
The LED anode is taken as the leg in the resistor's column and the cathode as the leg joined to ground, as in the schematic.
No USB cable is added, because the tutorial does not list one.
